thread:
alex: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we keep running into the same pain around pin metadata size for high-traffic tenants. thoughts?

sam: yep. main problem: we attach full rollout objects to the placement call and that bloats headers.

jordan: can we compress by sending only a stable-hash prefix + an affinity hint instead of the full model id?

lee: that helps, but resolver needs to handle prefix collisions. collisions are rare but must be deterministic.

maria: proposal: pinned_hash: "sha256:abcde..." but in request we send pinned_hash_prefix: "sha256:abcd" and affinity_score: 0.82. resolver tries full match then falls back to prefix resolution.

alex: showing a minimal example i pasted into the RFC notes last week:

```
{
  "pin_prefix": "sha256:abcd",
  "affinity": "0.82",
  "pin_ttl": "3600",
  "fallback_policy": "variant-order"
}
```

sam: two immediate tradeoffs: (1) decoding logic gets slightly more complex, (2) we need to log ambiguous prefix resolutions for observability.

jordan: also need an explicit tie-break rule: longest-match then lexicographic. otherwise different clients might pick different variants.

lee: agree. rule: resolver picks exact-id first, if none, picks longest prefix match. If multiple equal-length matches, pick highest affinity_score, then lexicographic.

maria: what about eviction semantics? pinned entries can age out; prefix-based pins might match retired models unexpectedly. we should add pin_epoch or pin_digest_version.

alex: add pin_digest_version string field — increments when model is force-rotated. request includes that so resolver can reject stale prefixes.

sam: that solves a class of weird rollbacks. also suggest a compact encoding for the header to avoid JSON in every request: base64(binary TLV) or a tiny proto.

jordan: TLV good. but ops needs readable logs. how about header contains small base64 blob, and gateway expands it into structured logs for telemetry.

lee: TL;DR of recommended shape: keep runtime header tiny (prefix + affinity + version), have control-plane provide full rollout objects via separate config sync. clients only need small hints.

maria: plus: add an explicit fallback_reason metric emitted when prefix resolution occurs so we can track frequency.

alex: deployment question — migration path: start accepting pin_prefix alongside full pin_id, but treat pin_prefix as advisory until we flip a feature flag. then flip for top 20 tenants first.

sam: ops checklist: add alert when prefix_resolve_rate > 0.5% of requests for a tenant, instrument ambiguous_resolve_count.

jordan: curious about canary behavior: if we roll a new model with same prefix (unlikely but possible for small prefixes), canary might route to new variant. recommend requiring 6+ hex chars (48 bits) as minimum prefix to make collisions astronomically unlikely.

lee: agreed. enforce min_prefix_len=6 in control-plane. add lint that refuses too-short prefixes in pin manifests.

maria: question on storage: do we store prefix-only pins in DB? i prefer storing canonical full-id and compute prefix on read for speed. avoids ambiguous writes.

alex: store full canonical id + precomputed prefixes of supported lengths. resolver uses indexed prefixes.

sam: action items: (1) add prefix fields to rollout schema draft, (2) add resolver tie-break rules to RFC, (3) implement TLV header prototype in gateway, (4) add telemetry metrics + alerts.

jordan: i'll take (2)+(4).

lee: i'll prototype TLV header encoder for gateway and shim for client-sdk.

maria: i'll update the rollout manifest writer and DB model to keep canonical-id + prefixes.

alex: i'll coordinate feature-flag rollout and spin up canary tenants.

deploy-bot: @alex started canary rollout for prefix-resolution-feature on dev cluster at 2024-11-12T15:02Z :rocket:

sam: thanks all. one more thing — we should add a short-term compatibility mode: if resolver sees a pin_prefix and a full pin_id header, prefer full pin_id. that lets older clients gradually ship.

jordan: good call. i'll add a test matrix for full-vs-prefix precedence.

lee: ok landing plan looks doable. filing follow-up PRs now. :thumbsup:

alex: perfect — i'll add the rollout checklist to the RFC thread. leaving notes about required observability and DB migration window.

maria: and put a hard limit on header size at the gateway so we don't regress again.

sam: agreed. closing this sync — will track PRs in the RFC. :handshake:
